citation: Dwamena A, Asadi Y, Gilstrap E, Wang H. Proteasomal dysfunction in the mouse forebrain induces mitochondrial DNA release, cGAS-STING signaling activation, and necroptosis. Journal of Neuropathology and Experimental Neurology. 2025. doi:10.1093/jnen/nlaf093.
description: Neuron-specific Psmc1 conditional knockout in mouse forebrain disrupted the 19S proteasome and activated inflammatory and necroptotic neuronal-death programs. It provides target-specific evidence that loss of this 19S ATPase can drive stress and degeneration in brain neurons.

citation: Yamada HY, Gorbsky GJ. Inhibition of TRIP1/S8/hSug1, a component of the human 19S proteasome, enhances mitotic apoptosis induced by spindle poisons. Molecular Cancer Therapeutics. 2006;5(1):29-38. doi:10.1158/1535-7163.MCT-05-0126.
description: Dominant-negative TRIP1/S8/hSug1, the human PSMC5 19S ATPase, reduced measurable proteasome activity, and siRNA-mediated hSug1 depletion reduced general proteasome activity. This supports the link from PSMC5 loss to proteasome impairment.

citation: Papa L, Gomes E, Rockwell P. Reactive oxygen species induced by proteasome inhibition in neuronal cells mediate mitochondrial dysfunction and a caspase-independent cell death. Apoptosis. 2007;12(8):1389-1405. doi:10.1007/s10495-007-0069-5.
description: Proteasome inhibition in mouse neuronal cells increased reactive oxygen species, Bax mitochondrial translocation, mitochondrial dysfunction, cytochrome c release, and cell death. It supplies the downstream neuronal stress direction expected after genetic disruption of PSMC-containing 19S proteasome function.

citation: Bae JE, Jang S, Kim JB, Hyung H, Park NY, Kim YH, Kim SH, Kim SH, Ha JM, Oh GS, Park K, Jeong K, Jang JS, Jo DS, Kim P, Lee HS, Ryoo ZY, Cho DH. Enhanced primary ciliogenesis via mitochondrial oxidative stress activates AKT to prevent neurotoxicity in HSPA9/mortalin-depleted SH-SY5Y cells. Molecular Brain. 2023;16:38. doi:10.1186/s13041-023-01029-7.
description: HSPA9/mortalin depletion in human SH-SY5Y neural cells increased mitochondrial fragmentation and mitochondrial reactive oxygen species and created a neurotoxic stress state. This is a target-specific but indirect bridge to the integrated mitochondrial and amino-acid stress genes observed after Hspa9 perturbation.

citation: van der Welle REN, Jobling R, Burns C, Sanza P, van der Beek JA, Fasano A, Chen L, Zwartkruis FJ, Zwakenberg S, Griffin EF, et al. Neurodegenerative VPS41 variants inhibit HOPS function and mTORC1-dependent TFEB/TFE3 regulation. EMBO Molecular Medicine. 2021;13:e13258. doi:10.15252/emmm.202013258.
description: Human VPS41 loss-of-function variants impaired HOPS function, delayed lysosomal delivery of endocytic and autophagic cargo, and altered mTORC1-dependent TFE3/TFEB-axis regulation. This links VPS41 loss to lysosomal transcriptional control but not directly to the single Mcoln1 increase in this screen.

citation: Li D, Shao R, Wang N, Zhou N, Du K, Shi J, Wang Y, Zhao Z, Ye X, Zhang X, Xu H. Sulforaphane activates a lysosome-dependent transcriptional program to mitigate oxidative stress. Autophagy. 2020;16(11):2055-2071. doi:10.1080/15548627.2020.1739442.
description: The study documents TFEB activation as a driver of autophagy and lysosomal gene expression and includes MCOLN1/TRPML1 in the TFEB/CLEAR lysosomal program. It completes a partial VPS41-to-TFEB-to-MCOLN1 bridge while leaving the sign and cell context uncertain.
